situation:
You are a community-college student who works night shifts at a parcel warehouse to stay enrolled. You have paid for two terms out of your own wages and have never borrowed money before. A credit union representative (judge) at ALDERGROVE COMMUNITY CREDIT UNION has agreed to meet with you about a tuition balance coming due in nine days.

The college business office will drop you from your spring classes unless the $780 balance is cleared by that date. CASHPOINT EXPRESS, the payday storefront across from campus, advertises on every bus shelter and will advance the full amount today, repaid as $940 in four weeks. The offer is licensed and its fees are disclosed as state law requires.

The $160 charge equals a month of your night-shift pay, and the storefront draws most of its revenue from students on this block. The credit union's small-dollar loan costs far less, and federal law lets you dispute the collections account listed on your credit report in error, but that dispute runs about thirty days, so you would miss the deadline and lose the term.

The business office will also negotiate a partial-payment extension, which adds a $75 late fee and blocks summer registration until the balance clears. The representative (judge) wants you to compare the paths and say which one you would take, explaining who carries the cost. The representative (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are a credit union representative (judge) at ALDERGROVE COMMUNITY CREDIT UNION. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You meet with members and neighbors who bring money questions to the branch, and this student has brought one with a deadline on it. You want to hear the three paths compared, hear which one the student would take, and hear plainly who ends up carrying the cost of that path.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Who ends up paying for the choice you recommended?
Is that a fair place for the cost to land?
